articles.title: Intrinsic backward emission of coherent Raman photons from homogeneous media
articles.authors: Jitendra Nath Acharyya, G. Benni, A. Sentenac, H. Rigneault, Sandro Heuke
articles.summary: In four-wave mixing the driving wavevectors set the output direction, so coherent Raman light can be sent backwards without any structure in the sample. The authors show that coherent Stokes Raman scattering (CSRS) phase-matches efficiently into the backward collection cone of a high-NA objective, and identify an azimuthally polarized Stokes annulus with a circularly polarized pump as the best geometry. With a ~790 nm pump and 1,030 nm Stokes, backward CSRS near 1,470 nm was detected on an InGaAs APD, giving about 7×10⁹ backward photons/s from sunflower oil. They imaged avocado, human fatty liver, sheep brain myelin and PMMA edges at ~330 nm lateral and 0.92 µm axial resolution. Backward flux is ~20× below forward CARS, narrowing to ~5× after detector efficiency.
articles.why: A refocusable coherent Raman signal that does not rely on sample scattering opens same-side detection for thick tissue, opaque substrates and fibre-based probes.

articles.title: Time-resolved infrared spectroscopy with entangled photons and visible-light detection
articles.authors: Jasleen Kaur, Yu Mukai, Ryo Okamoto, Shigeki Takeuchi
articles.summary: Time-resolved infrared (TR-IR) spectroscopy reveals molecular structural changes and charge-carrier dynamics on their intrinsic timescales, in photosynthesis, catalysis and optoelectronic materials, but requires complex sources of ultrashort infrared pulses, cryogenically cooled detectors to overcome thermal background, and intense probes that can perturb the sample. Quantum infrared spectroscopy avoids these constraints: harnessing quantum interference between the generation processes of frequency-entangled photon pairs, it reads out the infrared response of a sample by detecting only the visible partner photon, for which efficient detectors exist. …
articles.why: Brings quantum infrared spectroscopy into the time domain: entangled photon pairs read out a sample's infrared response by detecting only the visible partner photon, avoiding the ultrashort IR pulses, cryogenic detectors and intense probes that time-resolved IR normally needs.

articles.title: Quantum-logic spectroscopy of forbidden vibrational transitions in single nitrogen molecular ions
articles.authors: Aleksandr Shlykov, Meissa L. Diouf, Richard Karl, Mikolaj Roguski, Umesh Joshi, Stefan Willitsch
articles.summary: Electric-dipole forbidden spectroscopic transitions in atoms form the basis of many advanced implementations of quantum computers, atomic clocks and quantum sensors. Coherently addressing such transitions in molecules which are among the most ubiquitous and versatile quantum objects has remained a long-standing challenge owing to their complex energy-level structure. Here, we report the search, observation and coherent manipulation of electric-quadrupole rotational-vibrational transitions in single trapped molecules using a quantum-logic-spectroscopy protocol. …
articles.why: Uses a quantum-logic protocol to find, observe and coherently manipulate electric-quadrupole (dipole-forbidden) rotational-vibrational transitions in a single trapped N₂⁺ ion, bringing to molecules the kind of forbidden-transition control that underpins atomic clocks and quantum sensors.

articles.title: Ultra-broadband quantum infrared spectroscopy extending to 20 µm
articles.authors: Yu Mukai, Ryo Okamoto, Shigeki Takeuchi
articles.summary: Quantum infrared spectroscopy (QIRS), which exploits quantum interference between photon-pair generation processes, enables infrared spectroscopy using only visible and near-infrared (VNIR) light sources and detectors. Extending the spectral coverage of QIRS into the long-wavelength infrared region up to 20 µm is crucial for the identification and characterization of a broad range of materials. However, implementing QIRS beyond 10 µm has been challenging because the nonlinear materials used to date do not provide suitable photon-pair sources in this spectral region. …
articles.why: Quantum infrared spectroscopy measures IR absorption with only visible/near-IR lasers and detectors; extending it to 20 µm opens the long-wave region that photon-pair sources had not reached.

articles.title: Video-rate volumetric chemical imaging via mid-infrared photothermal optical diffraction tomography
articles.authors: Masato Fukushima, Keiichiro Toda, Yusei Sugawara, Shotaro Kawano, Takuro Ideguchi
articles.summary: Volumetric mid-infrared photothermal (MIP) imaging has been limited by a trade-off between speed and signal-to-noise. Pairing a high-power nanosecond mid-IR source with rapid angular scanning in optical diffraction tomography, the authors reach 19.2 volumes per second, roughly 400 times faster than earlier MIP tomography, with SNR above 70 and no temporal averaging. They track lipid droplets in 3D inside living cells and find heterogeneous, anomalous diffusion from full volumetric trajectories. Sweeping the mid-IR wavenumber gives hyperspectral volumes over a 300 cm⁻¹ window in about one second.
articles.why: About 400× faster than earlier mid-infrared photothermal tomography: 19 chemical volumes per second without averaging, enough to follow lipid droplets moving in 3D inside living cells.

articles.summary: Background Therapy-induced tissue alterations complicate intraoperative diagnosis of recurrent CNS tumors. We evaluated stimulated Raman histology (SRH) combined with convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for rapid tumor detection and classification. Methods In this bicentric observational study, fresh tissue from patients undergoing resection or stereotactic biopsy for suspected recurrent CNS tumors was imaged with fiber-laser-based SRH. CNN1 performed binary tumor/non-tumor prediction and CNN2 histotype classification. CNN1 was evaluated against blinded neuropathologist SRH consensus and CNN2 against the final integrated histopathological diagnosis. …
articles.why: Bicentric clinical study of fiber-laser SRH with CNNs on recurrent brain tumors, where therapy-induced changes make frozen sections hard to read; validated against blinded neuropathologists.

articles.title: Easy Access to Experimental Bond Dissociation Energies in Solution Using 2D-IR Spectroscopy
articles.authors: Kölbel J, Sévery L, Fernández-Terán RJ
institutions: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique
Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique et aux Énergies Alternatives
articles.summary: Bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of X─H bonds are central for the thermodynamics of proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET) and hydrogen-atom transfer (HAT) reactions, yet their direct determination in solution remains experimentally challenging. Established approaches rely on radical equilibration against reference compounds, or on multi-step thermodynamic cycles that compound experimental and computational uncertainties, and are often restricted to a narrow range of solvents. Here, we introduce two-dimensional infrared (2D-IR) spectroscopy as a direct spectroscopic route to BDFEs of main-group hydrides. …
articles.why: A direct spectroscopic route to X–H bond dissociation free energies in solution, replacing radical-equilibration and multi-step thermodynamic cycles; useful for PCET and HAT chemistry.

articles.title: Absolute Quantification of Tissue Composition by Raman Spectroscopy
articles.authors: Ersland EE, Mehrotra DR, Brisebois H, Han L, Grinstaff M, Schaer T, Bergholt MS, Snyder BD, Albro M
articles.summary: Raman spectroscopy captures the molecular fingerprints of living tissues without labels or tissue destruction. Translating these spectra into absolute measures of tissue biochemical composition remains a challenge owing to tissue-dependent optical properties, variations in sampling volume, and lack of normalization standards requisite for quantitative scaling. Here we introduce a scheme to derive the biochemical constituents of a tissue expressed as a percentage of the tissue wet weight, like biochemical assays, from Raman spectra measured optically. …
articles.why: Converts tissue Raman spectra into absolute composition (percent of wet weight, like a biochemical assay), addressing the normalization problem that keeps Raman semi-quantitative.

articles.title: Tip-enhanced vibrational ladder climbing in surface molecular system
articles.authors: Tatsuto Mochizuki, Shota Takahashi, Atsunori Sakurai, Toshiki Sugimoto
articles.summary: Achieving high-lying vibrational states is essential for actively controlling molecular reactions. We demonstrate vibrational ladder climbing of CO adsorbed on Pt(111) within the plasmonic tip-substrate nanogap formed in a scanning tunneling microscope, detected via tip-enhanced sum-frequency generation (TE-SFG). As the infrared pulse energy increases, hot-band peaks appear sequentially up to the 3-4 transition, indicating the stepwise population of higher vibrational states. Numerical analysis using the optical Bloch equations captures the observed energy dependence of these features. …
articles.why: Drives CO on Pt(111) up the vibrational ladder to the 3–4 transition inside an STM plasmonic nanogap, read out by tip-enhanced sum-frequency generation; reaching high-lying vibrational states locally is a step toward actively controlling surface reactions at the nanoscale.

articles.title: A-scan Raman microspectroscopy based on remote focusing with a planar mirror
articles.authors: Jisheng Zhang, Junjiang Liu, Pengfei Lai, Fuzhou Shen, Guanjingyun Wang, Xiangguo Yuan, Linyuan Zhao, Xingyun Wang, Huihong Wu, Daohong Xie, Ling-juan Zhang, Wenjie Liu, Quan Liu

articles.summary: Conventional depth-resolved Raman microspectroscopy relies on point-by-point axial scanning, which is slow and increases the risk of photodamage. To address this issue, we have developed A-scan Raman microspectroscopy, named after A-scan in ultrasound imaging, which is based on remote focusing with a planar mirror that maps the axial information of a sample into the lateral dimension for snapshot depth-resolved Raman measurements. Raman spectra from 21 distinct depth positions are captured simultaneously in a single snapshot. …
articles.why: Borrows the ultrasound A-scan idea: remote focusing maps depth onto the camera, giving Raman spectra from 21 depths in one snapshot instead of slow point-by-point axial scanning.

articles.summary: Wide-field mid-infrared photothermal (MIP) imaging enables chemically specific microscopy with submicron spatial resolution but remains fundamentally limited by the trade-off between field of view, mid-infrared pulse energy, and spectral tunability. As a result, current wide-field implementations are typically restricted to fields of view (FOVs) below 200 μm and to either the fingerprint or high-wavenumber spectral regions. …
articles.why: Pushes wide-field mid-infrared photothermal imaging past the usual sub-200 µm field of view to millimetre scale, with a picosecond OPO tunable across both fingerprint and high-wavenumber regions.

articles.title: Supercontinuum-driven broadband Fourier-transform photothermal microspectroscopy
articles.authors: Senyu Wang et al., Takuro Ideguchi
articles.summary: Photothermal microspectroscopy reads out local vibrational absorption through the heat it deposits, sensed by a separate optical probe, but broadband spectra are slow when the excitation laser has to be tuned step by step. The authors drive the measurement with a supercontinuum and record the photothermal signal through a rapid-scan interferometer, so the whole spectrum is obtained at once by Fourier transform. In the 1.65–2.35 µm window they record broadband photothermal spectra of aqueous samples at about one spectrum per second, and a dark-field detection scheme extends this to a single 6 µm polystyrene bead in water.
articles.why: Replaces step-by-step laser tuning with a supercontinuum and Fourier-transform readout, giving broadband photothermal vibrational spectra in about a second, including from a single microparticle in water.

articles.title: Frequency-swept Brillouin spectroscopy
articles.authors: Lin Kang, Shahrin Jahan Jaima, Jitao Zhang
articles.summary: Spontaneous Brillouin microscopy provides non-contact access to the viscoelastic properties of materials. Standard measurements typically utilize a single-wavelength continuous-wave laser to illuminate a specimen and excites a spontaneous Brillouin scattering signal, which is then recorded by a spectrometer. Existing Brillouin spectrometers are mostly built around either a scanning Fabry-Pérot etalon or a virtually imaged phased array (VIPA) etalon. While performing well, these setups are bulky and demand significant optical expertise to construct and maintain. Here, we propose a new approach to conducting Brillouin spectroscopy. …
articles.why: Replaces the bulky scanning Fabry–Pérot or VIPA spectrometer with a frequency-swept scheme, which could make Brillouin microscopy simpler to build and maintain.

articles.summary: Determining the chemical structure of a single molecule on a surface from spectroscopic data constitutes a challenging high-dimensional inverse problem. While tip-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (TERS) enables chemically specific imaging of single molecules with sub-nanometer spatial resolution, reconstructing complete molecular structures from TERS maps remains difficult due to ambiguous vibrational signatures and heavy reliance on expert interpretation. Here, we introduce TERS-ABNet, a deep-learning framework that reformulates single-molecule structure determination as an image-to-graph inference task. …
articles.why: Turns tip-enhanced Raman maps into complete single-molecule structures with deep learning (image-to-graph inference), reducing reliance on expert interpretation of ambiguous TERS signatures.

articles.title: Cavity-less Brillouin strong coupling in a solid-state continuous system
articles.authors: Laura Blázquez Martínez, Changlong Zhu, Birgit Stiller
institutions: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light
articles.summary: Strong coupling between two systems allows them to exchange coherent information before the systems decohere. This important regime in light–matter interactions has predominantly been reached in optical resonator configurations. Here we demonstrate strong coupling between optical and acoustic fields within a continuum of modes in a cavity-less configuration after a single pass through an optical waveguide. The underlying physical effect of anti-Stokes Brillouin–Mandelstam scattering in a highly nonlinear fibre at cryogenic temperature allows us to experimentally demonstrate strong coupling in a waveguide scenario. …
articles.why: Strong coupling between light and sound after a single pass through a cryogenic highly nonlinear fibre, with no optical resonator, via anti-Stokes Brillouin–Mandelstam scattering; extends a regime usually reserved for cavities to continuous waveguides.

articles.journal: Journal of Physical and Chemical Reference Data
articles.summary: The vibrational spectroscopy of isolated formic acid molecules, including both conformers and various isotopologs (H1, H2, C12, C13, O16), is compiled from the literature and critically reviewed. This work extends the previous database [Nejad and Sibert III, J. Chem. Phys. 154, 064301 (2021)] beyond 4000 cm−1 to include all available experimental band centers up to the near-infrared and visible regions. Assignments in the overtone region are reexamined using fc-CCSD(T) VPT2, resulting in five reassignments for HCOOH, three for its deuterated isotopologs, and one for H13COOH. The implications of the present work for the HITRAN database are discussed and directions for future work outlined.

articles.summary: Chemical transformations at biological interfaces are central to cellular function, yet the weak vibrational signals associated with subtle molecular changes limit their spatially resolved observation. Here, we present metasurface-driven mid-infrared photothermal imaging (MetaMIP), which uses resonantly engineered metasurfaces to amplify molecular temperature modulation while retaining rapid thermal recovery. Visible-light detection converts this response into submicrometre maps of individual nanoparticles and biological cells. In living cells, MetaMIP resolves spatially distinct chemical changes during enzymatic lipid conversion across the cell membrane. …
articles.why: Resonant metasurfaces amplify the photothermal signal while keeping fast thermal recovery, so weak vibrational changes at the cell membrane can be imaged in living cells during an enzymatic lipid conversion.

articles.summary: High-dimensional microscopy captures features across space, time, and spectrum, but complex backgrounds obscure signals. institutions: Max-Born-Institute for Nonlinear Optics and Short Pulse Spectroscopy
articles.summary: Coherent control uses interference between quantum pathways to enhance or suppress transitions to a target quantum state. In stimulated Raman excitation, such control can be achieved through interference between two indistinguishable pathways connecting the same initial and final states, with the relative phase between the pathways modulating the population transfer to the final state. Extending this strategy to the extreme ultraviolet (XUV) and X-ray regimes would enable control of ultrafast electronic dynamics and site-selective core excitations. …

institutions: Institute of Nuclear & Radiological Sciences and Technology, Energy & Safety
articles.summary: Raman spectroscopy generates large volumes of unlabeled data that are difficult to exploit with conventional supervised learning. This work introduces a multi-domain self-supervised learning framework based on a masked autoencoder (MAE) for learning transferable Raman spectral representations from heterogeneous biological, chemical, forensic, and materials datasets. The proposed pretraining strategy incorporates physics-aware objectives by combining masked intensity reconstruction with a sparse Voigt-profile decoder that models spectral peak structure through differentiable peak centers, widths, and amplitudes. …

articles.title: Raman Spectroscopy of Laser-Micro-Annealing-Induced Structural Changes in Ti-6Al-4V
articles.authors: Hilde Helen Hardtdegen, M. Mikulics, Ralf Eickhoff, Steffen Antusch, Joachim Mayer, Thomas Hanemann
articles.summary: This short study presents the results of micro-Raman investigations performed on the alloy Ti-6Al-4V, which was additively manufactured via metal fused filament fabrication (MF3). Local laser micro-annealing was applied at different power intensities to distinct regions. The applied laser power density was varied in the range of ~0.05 kW/cm2 to ~5 MW/cm2. Laser-induced compositional changes in structures, approx. 1 µm in diameter, arranged in an array, are laterally limited. Simultaneously, the surrounding matrix maintains its initial pristine material properties down to ~500 nm in spacing between neighboring structures, reproducibly. …

articles.title: Bottom-Up Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering for the Detection of Micro-Objects and Globular Analytes
articles.authors: Andrey Karlovich Sarychev, Milena S. Shestopalova, Denis S. Korzhov, Andrey V. Ivanov, I. V. Bykov, Konstantin N. Afanas'ev, Nikita Osipov, Dmitry V. Basmanov, В. А. Олейников, Konstantin E. Mochalov
articles.summary: Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is typically achieved by depositing the analyte on a metal or semiconductor substrate. We propose a bottom-up approach, enabling SERS by depositing a metal on the surface of the object being studied. A Mie-theory analysis of electric-field enhancement in dielectric core-shell particles is presented. A correlative approach combining SERS, atomic force microscopy, and scanning electron microscopy is employed to model the conditions required for sensitive SERS detection and spectral analysis of polystyrene microspheres (PMSs) as models of globular and vesicle-like objects. …

articles.title: Computational design of a TiO2 nanopillar metalens at 785nm for compact light emitting diode (LED) Raman excitation
articles.authors: Perry Neil Fernandez, Froilan E. De Guzman, Francis Sanots Dela Cruz, Romeric F. Pobre
articles.summary: Light emitting diodes (LEDs) are an inexpensive and robust excitation source for portable Raman spectrometers, but their Lambertian emission has to be collected by millimetre-scale refractive optics that dominate the size and alignment budget of the instrument. A flat dielectric metasurface bonded directly to the LED die would remove this bottleneck, provided the meta-atom platform combines full phase coverage with low loss at the working wavelength. Here we report the computational design and scalar wave-optical assessment of a TiO2-on-SiO2 nanopillar metalens for a 785nm LED-pumped Raman source. …

articles.title: Amide I kurtosis maps cardiac amyloid in human tissue by ultrabroadband multiplex coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS) microscopy
articles.authors: Koki Ota, Ting-Hao Chen, Takanori Yamaguchi, Toyokazu Otsubo, Yusuke Murakami, Minori Masaki, Philippe Leproux, Ryo Suzuki, Koichi Node, Hideaki Kano
articles.summary: Cardiac amyloidosis is caused by deposits of misfolded proteins in the heart and can lead to heart failure. Histological confirmation typically involves staining tissue sections with Congo red and examining them under polarized light for apple-green birefringence; however, achieving an interpretable, label-free, and observer-independent assessment remains challenging. Here we show that Pearson kurtosis of channel intensities within the amide I window provides an interpretable, fitting-free contrast for cardiac amyloid in unstained human cardiac tissue sections from ten participants imaged by ultrabroadband multiplex coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS). …

articles.title: All-optical deconvolution via quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy with bright twin beams
articles.authors: Yujiro Eto
institutions: Center for Science Adventure and Collaborative Research Advancement
articles.summary: The resolution of spectroscopic measurements is fundamentally limited by the convolution between a system's intrinsic response and the instrument response function, creating an ill-posed inverse problem. While entangled photons can theoretically bypass these limits, low photon flux has hindered their experimental realization. Here, we propose quantum cross-correlation spectroscopy (QCCS), utilizing macroscopic twin beams (signal and idler beams) to physically circumvent this convolution limit in coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering. …

articles.title: Quantum Information-Theoretic Analysis of Optical Fiber Sensing via Stimulated Brillouin Scattering
articles.authors: Kiran Adhikari, Janis Nötzel
articles.summary: Stimulated Brillouin scattering (SBS) is a powerful mechanism for distributed sensing in optical fibers, as the Brillouin response is highly sensitive to local material parameters. Assuming the input probe is a quantum state, we develop a quantum-information-theoretic framework for SBS-based fiber sensing and intrusion detection. Starting from a linearized opto-acoustic Hamiltonian, we derive an effective input-output relation for a short fiber segment. We then model each fiber segment as a single-mode bosonic Gaussian channel and the entire fiber as a cascade of quantum channels. …

articles.summary: Investigation of the interactions of methane with metal oxides is crucial for elucidating absorption configurations at active sites of catalysts, which has proven to be a challenging experimental target due to the difficulty in size selection of neutral systems. In this work, the interactions of methane with rare earth metal oxides are studied by using size-specific infrared-vacuum ultraviolet spectroscopy and quantum chemical calculations. Two distinct configurations of methane adsorption are found in the MO(CH4)n (M = Ce, Y; n = 1-3) complexes. …

articles.summary: Proteinuria, defined by an abnormally elevated concentration of proteins in the urine, serves as a critical biomarker for the early detection and diagnosis of preeclampsia. Elevated proteinuria levels adversely affect both maternal and foetal health, increasing the risk of preterm birth and low birth weight. This study focused on the identification of proteinuria in blood samples through Fourier‐transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy as a diagnostic tool for real‐time diagnosis. Blood plasma collected during birth was evaluated in four study groups: pregnant controls ( n = 12), pregnant women with proteinuria ( n = 13), newborn controls ( n = 12), newborns with proteinuria ( n = 14). …

Jet-cooled spectra were recorded using two complementary setups: a continuous supersonic jet coupled to the Fourier transform spectrometer of the AILES beamline at the SOLEIL synchrotron facility (Jet-AILES) and a quantum cascade laser spectrometer coupled to a pulsed jet (SPIRALES). These measurements were combined with long-path cell spectra at room temperature and supported by anharmonic quantum chemical calculations. …

articles.title: ZooMS-referenced analytical assessment of vibrational taxonomic markers in museum ivory
articles.authors: Xiaodan Yang, Binjie Qi, Meiting Yan, Xiaoguang Li, Yanju Kong, Zihua Tang
institutions: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
articles.summary: Species-level identification of elephant ivory is important for museum documentation, provenance research, and the interpretation of worked ivory objects. Previous studies have proposed a range of FTIR- and Raman-based spectral features as potentially taxon-associated, but their reliability in museum materials remains uncertain. Here, we reassess these previously proposed vibrational-spectroscopic criteria using ten conservation-derived ivory dowels from a Qing dynasty table screen in the Palace Museum, with Zooarchaeology by Mass Spectrometry (ZooMS) providing independent taxonomic identifications. …

articles.title: Investigation of Lamotrigine Crystal Polymorphs Using Crystal Structure Prediction and Terahertz Spectroscopy
articles.authors: Salvatore Zarrella, Mizuki Mohara, Kei Shimura, Timothy M. Korter
articles.summary: Crystal structure prediction (CSP) plays a significant role in exploring the crystal polymorphism of pharmaceutical solids. Determination of the atomic-level structures of crystalline materials is a fundamental step in understanding their bulk physical and chemical properties and behavior in drug products. CSP can be performed using numerous computational approaches, but all ultimately require comparison with experimental measurements to confirm the CSP findings. In this work, terahertz (THz) vibrational spectroscopy is combined with powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) to demonstrate a new metrics framework for the validation of CSP investigations. …

articles.title: Conformational heterogeneity and vibrational signatures of dAMP in aqueous solution revealed by high-accuracy machine-learning potentials

institutions: S.N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences
articles.summary: Nucleotides are the fundamental building blocks of life, yet many aspects of their behavior and interactions in water remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the structural and vibrational properties of 2^{{\prime} } 2 ′ -deoxyadenosine 5^{{\prime} } 5 ′ -monophosphate (dAMP) in aqueous solution using a machine-learning approach supported by IR spectroscopy experiments. We develop highly accurate neural network potentials through an active-learning protocol that systematically samples the free-energy landscape at the GGA level and efficiently transfers this information to higher levels of theory. This potential accurately describes dAMP in water over nanosecond timescales. …

articles.title: Mineralogical and Elemental Variability of Canine Dental Calculi Reveals an Age-Associated Calcite–Apatite Continuum
articles.authors: Marcello Campione, Andrea Lucotti, Matteo Tommasini, Claudio Pezzoli, Valerio Cerantola, Capitani Giancarlo
articles.summary: Dental calculus is a mineralized oral biofilm widely occurring in domestic dogs, yet its mineralogical variability and chemical evolution remain insufficiently defined. Here, we investigate dental calculus collected as biological waste material during routine professional dental cleaning from twenty-eight indoor pet dogs of different breeds, ages, and clinical backgrounds. X-ray powder diffraction, vibrational spectroscopy, and elemental analysis were combined to determine the crystalline phase assemblage, phosphate and carbonate spectral signatures, and major-element composition of the deposits. …

articles.title: Zero-quantum dual-comb spectroscopy of collective resonances in rubidium vapor
articles.authors: Bachana Lomsadze, Johnason Yao, Hankang Gao, Roman Junes
articles.summary: We report dual-comb spectroscopy of the collective zero-quantum response of rubidium atoms. The observed signals include two-atom collective resonances at 2( ω D 2 − ω D 1 ), ω 5 P 3/2 →5 D − ω D 2 , ω 5 P 3/2 →5 D − ω D 1 , and ( ω D 2 − ω D 1 )+( ω 5 P 3/2 →5 D − ω D 1 ), as well as higher-order three-atom resonances. Unlike double-quantum spectroscopy, which probes sum-frequency resonances of multiple atoms, the zero-quantum pathway probes difference-frequency correlations between optical transitions. …

articles.title: Vibrationally inelastic scattering of NO from metal surfaces: A partial mean-field approach
articles.authors: Zhiyan Liu, Hengyue Zhang, Qiang Shi
institutions: Beijing National Laboratory for Molecular Sciences
articles.summary: Vibrationally inelastic scattering of NO from metal surfaces probes electronically nonadiabatic molecule-surface dynamics. Experiments have reported multi-quantum relaxation and a work function dependence associated with transient charge transfer. In this work, we develop a partial mean-field approach for a Newns-Anderson model of NO scattering. The molecule-surface distance is treated classically using the mean-field approach, whereas the NO stretch, molecular electronic states, and metal electron bath are treated quantum mechanically with fermionic hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM). …

articles.title: Laser-Induced Fluorescence Hyperspectral Imaging for Classification of Coastal Macroalgae, Eelgrass, and Mussels

articles.summary: This study explores the application of fluorescence hyperspectral imaging (FHSI) for marine ecosystem monitoring, combining laser-induced fluorescence (LIF) with hyperspectral imaging (HSI), an approach rarely applied in marine ecology. Photopigments such as chlorophylls, carotenoids, and phycobiliproteins emit distinct fluorescence signals when excited at specific wavelengths. Species-discriminating spectral signatures can then address persistent challenges in benthic monitoring, including overlapping optical properties among species and complex underwater conditions. …

articles.authors: Diana Marcela Montoya, I.J. Paez-Mila, Carlos Fabián Arias‐Ramos, C. L. Gómez-Heredia, Yulieth Catherine Reyes Roa, Juan Carlos Salcedo-Reyes, Hailin Zhao Hu, J.A. Ramírez-Rincón

The films have been fabricated under ambient laboratory conditions (relative humidity > 40% without glovebox) by spin coating and bar coating, with areas of 6.25 and 25 cm 2 respectively. Over a 16-week monitoring period, spatially and spectrally resolved HSI data have been used to establish a correlation between perovskite quality and changes in optical transmittance across the 450-975 nm spectral range. …

articles.authors: Martin Hohmann
articles.summary: Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) of turbid, tissue-mimicking media entangles the geometry of subsurface inclusions with the optical properties of the surrounding matrix in every spectrum. From HSI cubes of polyurethane phantoms with obliquely drilled inclusions we recover two physically distinct quantities: a dense depth map of the inclusion and the scalar iso-point wavelength, the point of near-invariance at which the depth-dependent modulation of the diffuse reflectance cancels. …

articles.title: Validation of video-rate laparoscopic multispectral imaging systems for quantitative bowel perfusion assessment using a hyperspectral reference in a porcine model
articles.authors: Denis Gholami Bajestani, Peggy Stock, Sandra Nickel, Annekatrin Pfahl, H. Köhler, Haukur Sigmarsson, Johannes Kauffold, Andreas Melzer, Hans‐Michael Tautenhahn
articles.summary: Quantitative assessment of bowel perfusion remains challenging during minimally invasive surgery. This study investigated whether video-rate laparoscopic multispectral imaging can provide contrast-agent-free perfusion assessment under intra-abdominal conditions. Ten pigs were examined in vivo. Regions of the small bowel were imaged during baseline perfusion, partial vascular occlusion, and complete ischemia. Matched measurements were acquired using two prototype laparoscopic multispectral imaging systems and the approved TIVITA Mini hyperspectral imaging system as reference. The first system was evaluated in six animals and the second in four. …

articles.title: Chronology and function of Tangbaletasi cave paintings via hyperspectral and iconographic analyses
articles.authors: Fengyi Huang, Yihao Fu, Guisheng Zhou, Lu Li, Chai Yue, Cheng Liu, Jun Wang, Jinye Peng, Baheti Zhuoya
articles.summary: The Tangbaletasi Cave Paintings in the Altai region of Xinjiang comprise a diverse assemblage of images preserved on natural cave walls. This study integrates hyperspectral imaging, iconographic comparison, spatial context, and historical sources to investigate the chronology, composition, and potential functions of the paintings. The rock art dominated by anthropomorphic figures and geometric motifs can be broadly attributed to the Bronze Age. The overall spatial configuration of the cave suggests the presence of organized, non-domestic activities. …

articles.title: UV Fluorescence Sensing of Medical-Chemical-and- Biological Analytes by an AlGaN/Si-on-Sapphire Optoelectronic Chip
articles.authors: Richard Soref
articles.summary: This paper proposes and analyzes a compact fluorescence-photometer lab-on-a-chip that is simpler than a fluorescence spectrometer, and that does not require spectrum reconstruction by a computer. An on-chip AlGaN VCSEL lasing at 280 nm, or at 310 nm, pumps an on-chip sample in the form of liquid or solid or tissue, thereby exciting signature fluorescence in the 300 to 540 nm wavelength range. This emission signal is detected and read out by an on-chip UV-enhanced Silicon photodiode. The 2 cm x 5 cm chip consists of C-plane (0001) Sapphire, and no lenses, prisms, or mirrors are utilized in the photometer. …

articles.title: Raman Thermometry of Confined Gas Milli-Flows
articles.authors: G. Tejeda, César Sosa Álvarez, J. M. Fernández
institutions: Instituto de Estructura de la Materia
articles.summary: The temperature of rarefied gas flows inside small channels is hard to measure without disturbing the flow. We present here an optical approach with submillimeter spatial resolution, based on Raman spectroscopy, and several examples of its application to gas flows within millimeter-sized channels. For this work, we have designed and built several channels with different geometries, and forced thermal gradients between some of their surfaces while flowing N2, CO2 and H2 through the channels. The pressures ranged from atmospheric down to 11 mbar, and the flow velocities ranged from 8 to over 450 cm/s. The most rarefied flows lie in the slip regime (Kn ≥0.001). …

articles.title: Illuminating Streptomyces : Raman Spectroscopy for Antibiotic Detection and Monitoring
articles.authors: Adéla Mikulová, Jan Bobek, Martin Kizovský, Markéta Benešová, Ota Samek, Pavlína Modlitbová, Zdeněk Pilát
institutions: Czech Academy of Sciences, Institute of Scientific Instruments
articles.summary: The genus Streptomyces is well known as a prolific source of many bioactive compounds. This review outlines the principles of Raman spectroscopy and its application to bacterial systems, with particular emphasis on the secondary metabolites produced by Streptomyces . Streptomyces are unparalleled chemical factories, producing over two‐thirds of all naturally derived antibiotics and bioactive molecules. Incorporating Raman spectroscopy into the study of these secondary metabolites offers a non‐destructive, label‐free method to monitor chemical diversity in real time. …

articles.authors: Yi-Hao Chen, Wenchao Wang, 侯绍东, José Enrique Antonio-Lopez, Rodrigo Amezcua‐Correa, Chris Xu, Frank W. Wise
articles.summary: Raman scattering underlies a broad range of spectroscopic and light-generation techniques, yet its conventional description, based on the Raman gain spectrum, accurately describes only long-pulse, steady-state dynamics. We employ a time-domain theoretical approach to account for spectrotemporal aspects of continuous frequency-shifting, which are not addressed by prior theories. In particular, molecules with strong Raman responses do not produce an efficient soliton self-frequency shift in gas-filled hollow-core fibers. …

articles.title: Diamond Raman laser for hydroxyl radical planar laser-induced fluorescence
articles.authors: Boris Leonov, Richard Mildren
articles.summary: This Letter describes, to the best of our knowledge, the first application of an Nd:YAG-pumped diamond Raman laser (DRL) for OH planar laser-induced fluorescence (PLIF). DRL was used to convert 532 nm pump radiation into 573 nm output, corresponding to the 1 st Stokes Raman shift, via the stimulated Raman scattering process in a diamond crystal, with an achieved conversion efficiency of 52%. The 573 nm output was then doubled to generate the UV radiation targeting the Q 1 (14) OH transition near 286.5 nm. The overall conversion efficiency from 532 nm pump to 286.5 nm UV output was recorded at 5%. This demonstration was performed in methane/air combustion produced by a Hencken burner. …

articles.title: Observing Elusive Reaction Intermediates with Raman Spectroscopy via Melt-React-Trap
articles.authors: Lucille Kuster, Mathieu Frenette
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.summary: Understanding reaction pathways relies on detecting and characterizing reactive and short-lived intermediate species. Melt-React-Trap (MRT) is introduced as a technique to generate and identify such elusive species via Raman microscopy. This method combines the advantages of low-temperature spectroscopy, rendering convenient the measurement of unstable molecules, with localized heating to allow thermal reactions. Using this approach, reagents are sequentially frozen, mixed in a cryomill and held under cryogenic conditions. A high-power focused Raman laser can locally melt this mixture and allow the reagents to react. …

articles.title: Time-Dependent Molecular Changes in Preserved Rat Corneas Revealed by Raman Spectroscopy
articles.authors: Hüseyin Kaya, Mustafa Ünal
articles.summary: Corneal transplantation depends on donor tissue that is stored before use, yet routine assessment of stored corneas relies on structural measures that do not describe the biochemical state of the tissue. In this study, Raman spectroscopy was used to follow molecular changes in rat corneas across 14 days of hypothermic storage. Eighty-four corneas were obtained from 84 Wistar albino rats, assigned to 14 groups according to storage duration, and kept in corneal preservation solution at +4 °C. Harvest was staggered across consecutive days so that all spectra could be acquired in a single session. …

articles.authors: Maria Gancheva, I. Koseva, Rosica Petrova, Надя Петрова, Tsvetomila Lazarova
institutions: Institute of General and Inorganic Chemistry
articles.summary: IR and Raman spectra of pure and chromium doped glasses and glass–ceramics from the system Li2O-CaO-GeO2-B2O3 are investigated and analyzed. The IR spectra of the pure and chromium doped glass samples contain bands typical of germanate and borate glasses. The amorphous network in the undoped glass is built by deformed GeO4 tetrahedra, BO3 groups and LiO4 tetrahedra. Doping with 0.5 at% Cr2O3 leads to the appearance of BO4 groups and an increase in the symmetry of the GeO4 groups. The bands associated with chromium are not observed. The comparison between glass and glass–ceramic IR spectra shows the more intensive bands in the latter. …

articles.authors: Jesper Laurberg Sand, Minna Groenning, Erik Skibsted, Anders Kristensen
articles.summary: Shifted excitation Raman difference spectroscopy (SERDS) is a method for eliminating fluorescence in Stokes Raman spectra, typically used when computational pre-processing methods can no longer yield any further information. However, the choice of the magnitude of the excitation laser wavenumber shift induces a systematic variation in the results. In this paper, we present a mathematical model that precisely describes how measured peak positions and heights depend on the choice of the wavenumber shift. …

articles.title: Real-time classification of waste polyethylene using terahertz and raman spectroscopy integrated machine learning
articles.authors: Marco Herbsommer, Seongmin Yoon, Mahavir Singh, Sushrut Karmarkar, Meghana Sudarshan, Christopher J. Welch, Vikas Tomar

This study presents an in-operation machine-learning (ML) approach combining terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) and Raman spectroscopy for rapid classification of industrial polyethylene (PE)-rich waste feedstocks. Spectral data from six industry-provided PE-rich materials with differences in additives and physical form were collected to build a dual-modality spectral library. …

articles.authors: William Davis, Bipin Kumar, Osama Terra, Adam Sharp, Richard Mildren
articles.summary: Continuous-wave Raman lasers are emerging as promising light sources that combine their characteristic wavelength conversion with low quantum-limited frequency noise, making them attractive for quantum and sensing applications. Linewidth studies so far have been based on free-space Raman crystal lasers, with linewidth limited by technical noise due to vibrations and air currents. A 1064 nm pump is actively locked to the cavity using the Pound–Drever–Hall technique, generating Stokes emission at 1174 nm with a threshold pump power of 260 mW. …

articles.title: Complementary Raman and ToF-SIMS analysis of oxide and fluoride networks in LiF corrosion of Inconel 625
articles.authors: Aida Nikbakht, Maciej Bik, Christine Geers
articles.summary: This study investigates the corrosion scale formed on Inconel 625 exposed to LiF in air at 600°C for 168 h and 1000 h, using confocal Raman spectroscopy in combination with SEM-EDS, ToF-SIMS, and XRD. After longer exposures, LiCrO2 formed at the interface between the spinel zone and chromia, indicating progressive lithiation and partial transformation of the protective oxide. …

articles.authors: María de Los Ángeles Martínez Arcos, Antonio J. Sarabia, Jorge Peláez Castillo, Belén Martínez Moral, Juan Carlos Fernández, David Moreno‐González, Marı́a Isabel Torres, Ricardo Rivera Fernández, Antonio Peñas, Jorge Nicolás Dominguez

We applied a digestion-filtration protocol coupled to untargeted single-particle confocal Raman microspectroscopy to pre-procedural peripheral venous blood (8.0–10.0 mL per venipuncture) from eight healthy controls and six patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). …

By utilizing circularly or elliptically polarized 1030-nm, 800-fs driving pulses, we excite a cross-circularly polarized Raman process that effectively breaks the phase-matched four-wave mixing coupling. This mechanism allows Raman gain to dominate, driving a discrete energy transfer to Stokes waves that produces a significantly stronger and highly asymmetric spectral redshift compared to linear polarization. Simply varying the input energy allows the redshifted spectral lobe to be continuously tuned from 1040 to 1100 nm. …

Within the United States, the Drug Enforcement Administration seizes tens of thousands of kg of clandestine powders, tablets, crystals, and liquids that may contain anywhere from 1−100% pure methamphetamine every year. The aim of this study was to evaluate the performance of the commercial Artificial Intelligent Raman Microbial Analyzer for Biology (AIRMAB) for the rapid clinical identification of swine bacterial pathogens. …

articles.title: Revealing the Nature of the Charge Density Wave Order of ErTe_{3} via Raman Scattering under Anisotropic Strain
articles.authors: Freitas T, Udina M, Alekhin A, Nilforoushan N, Houver S, Sacuto A, Gonzalez BA, Fisher IR, Paul I, Gallais Y
institutions: Stanford Institute for Materials and Energy Sciences
articles.summary: The nature of the charge density wave (CDW) order of the rare-earth tritelluride ErTe_{3} is investigated by Raman scattering under anisotropic strain. The CDW state of ErTe_{3} is unconventional since it is accompanied by an unusual mirror symmetry breaking, whose origin remains to be understood. Studying the polarization-resolved Raman spectrum of the CDW amplitude mode as a function of strain and temperature, we find that the mirror symmetry breakings of the CDW state are not independent, arguing against the recently proposed ferroaxial multicomponent CDW order. …

articles.title: Vibrational spectroscopy of microorganisms: A review
articles.authors: McGoverin C
institutions: Dodd-Walls Centre for Photonic and Quantum Technologies
articles.summary: Vibrational spectroscopic methods, mid- and near-infrared, and Raman spectroscopies, have been extensively applied to the study of microorganisms. This is due to the relatively rapid analysis time, relative low-cost, experimental flexibility, and phenotypic nature of these methods. Consequently, vibrational spectroscopies have been investigated for clinical, environmental and industrial microbiology applications. This review outlines the principles of mid- and near-infrared, and Raman spectroscopies, and steps through vibrational spectroscopic experiments in the context of microbiological studies. …

articles.title: Data-Driven Inverse Design Method for Photonic Crystal Fibers and Its Application to Near-Infrared Flat Supercontinuum Control
articles.authors: Lanxin Wei
articles.journal: Journal of Intelligence and Knowledge Engineering
articles.summary: To overcome the issues of traditional photonic crystal fiber (PCF) design methods, such as the need for trial-and-error, low efficiency, and inability to adequately meet diverse spectral requirements, this paper proposes a big data-driven inverse design method. This method inversely derives the optimal PCF structural parameters based on a target spectrum, thereby enabling precise control to achieve a flat supercontinuum (SC) in the near-infrared (NIR) range. A large number of different structures are simulated using the finite element method (FEM) to generate a "structure–property" sample set. …

articles.title: Evaluating and optimizing Raman analytical protocols for CO2 fluids
articles.authors: Penny E. Wieser, Charlotte L. DeVitre, Isabelle Susman
articles.summary: Raman spectroscopy is widely used to quantify CO2 density in geological fluids, yet acquisition parameters, spectral processing methodologies and densimeter calibrations vary between laboratories. The precision of Raman CO2 measurements, and the broader applicability of densimeters generated for a specific instrument, are still debated. This study describes a series of experiments to investigate the effect of different instrument and acquisition parameters on CO2 densities and their errors that can be performed on different Raman instruments, allowing users to determine analytical best practices. …

articles.title: A dataset of Raman spectra with quantitative labels of mixtures of nitrate, nitrite and sulphate
articles.authors: Luciani L, Nocera A, Raimondi M, Sbrollini A, Morettini M, Galassi R
articles.summary: This article describes a dataset of Raman spectra acquired from aqueous solutions containing nitrate, nitrite, and sulphate ions at known concentration levels. The dataset includes 694 raw Raman spectra collected in the Stokes region from 400 to 3900 cm⁻¹, and each spectrum is associated with quantitative labels reporting the concentrations of nitrate, nitrite, and sulphate in mg/L. The data include single-analyte, binary-mixture, and ternary-mixture samples, covering a range of concentration values for the three target anions. …
